newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps weaken with crude, naphtha static.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps weaken with crude, naphtha static.

text.p: European oil swaps were easier on Tuesday after crude started to head southwards.
Brent crude CFDs were thinly talked in the morning, with values easing in a parallel motion with weaker IPE futures.
The balance of this week eased down one cent or so to 19 cents under July while next week was 21.50 cents under July. A June 12-18 deal was concluded at August -26 cents.
Gasoline, which gained on Monday in a catch-up play with crude's rises on Friday, eased back on Tuesday by at least $2.00 a tonne.
June was heard offered at $208 compared yesterday's $210 with bids down to $206.50 from $209. Further out values extended backwardation with July $6 under June and August $9 below.
Physical barges were concluded at $207 and $207.25 fob ARA.

Naphtha was essentially unchanged with traders saying the sector was pausing while it assessed crude's stance. Some said the expectation had been that crude would come off further. June was talked at $190.75-$191.25 with July pegged at $191.50-192.00.
Heavy fuel lost ground with July offered at $86.50 having briefly touched $86.75 earlier. June was pegged around $85.50, about $1 weaker than Monday.
Low sulphur swaps were steady with June around $96.50 although nothing was heard done.
